records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Net sales decreased 6% due to a decline in Wine and Spirits net sales led by a decrease in organic branded shipment volume and a decrease in Beer net sales driven primarily by a shipment volume decline, partially offset by a favorable impact from pricing.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: The decrease in Beer net sales is due to (i) a $75.7 million decrease in shipment volume and (ii) $7.5 million of unfavorable product mix primarily from a shift in package types, partially offset by $44.9 million of

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Largely in connection with the 2025 Wine Divestitures we recognized contract liabilities and inventory obsolescence expenses, partially offset by changes in net assets held for sale (First Quarter 2026).

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Our business strategy for the Wine and Spirits segment continues to focus on delivering growth and improving margins beyond Fiscal 2026 by driving our higher-end brands and operating efficiencies.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Operating income decreased 24% primarily due to (i) unfavorable Comparable Adjustments led by losses associated with assets held for sale impairment and related expenses as well as losses recognized on undesignated commodity derivative contracts for First Quarter 2026 compared with gains for First Quarter 2025 and (ii) the declines in Wine and Spirits and Beer segments net sales, partially offset by a successful execution of cost initiatives within the Beer segment.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: In fiscal year 2024, approximately 39% of our sales were generated outside of the U.S. We also are partners in a number of joint ventures involved in the manufacture and sale of flavorful products, the most significant of which is McCormick de Mexico.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: •Volume and product mix favorably impacted net sales by 1.3%.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: The decrease in operating cash flow was primarily driven by higher cash used for working capital primarily driven by accounts payable decreases driven by the timing of inventory purchases.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: In the second quarter of 2025, our gross profit margin decreased by 20 basis points primarily driven by increased commodity costs.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Operating income was $245.8 million in the second quarter of 2025, compared to $234.1 million in the same period of 2024, reflecting an increase of 5.0%.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: When combined with the operating efficiencies achieved by volume purchasing, efficient distribution and reduced handling of merchandise in no-frills, self-service warehouse facilities, these volumes and turnover enable us to operate profitably at significantly lower gross margins (net sales less merchandise costs) than most other retailers.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: •Net sales increased 8% to $61,965, driven by an increase in comparable sales and sales at 29 net new warehouses opened since the end of the third quarter of 2024;

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Changes in our net investment in merchandise inventories (the difference between merchandise inventories and accounts payable) is impacted by several factors, including inventory levels and turnover, payment terms with suppliers, and early payments to obtain discounts.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Net sales growth and gross margins are also impacted by our competition, which is vigorous and widespread, across a wide range of global, national and regional wholesalers and retailers, including those with e-commerce operations.

records.title: 10-Q
records.text: Negative aspects of such growth include lower initial operating profitability relative to existing warehouses and cannibalization of sales at existing warehouses when openings occur in existing markets.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Revenue was flat in 2025 primarily due to increased base yields at both of our transportation segments and higher volume at Federal Express, which offset two fewer operating days at both of our transportation segments, lower shipments and fuel surcharges at FedEx Freight, and unfavorable currency exchange rates.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Consequently, this environment has led to lower shipments at FedEx Freight, negatively affecting our results in 2025.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Partially offsetting these pressures were continued savings related to DRIVE and higher demand for international economy and U.S. ground package services.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Lower fuel prices negatively affected yields through lower fuel surcharges at FedEx Freight and reduced fuel expense at both of our transportation segments during 2025.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Operating income declined in 2025 primarily due to lower shipments and fuel surcharges at FedEx Freight, a continued mix shift toward deferred package services which constrained yield growth, and the expiration of our contract with the U.S. Postal Service ("USPS").
